eras.label: Historical
eras.note: Represented in documents, memories, archives and events only. Consumes no action slot and cannot be commanded, because the person is dead. Per the issue's own MVP distinction.

eras.label: Present
eras.note: Alive and reachable in the scenario. Being agentic is not the same as holding a council seat: an independent patron is not automatically one of a faction's four leaders.

dynasty.role: founding shipping magnate; Victorian-era head of the family firm
dynasty.what_the_scenario_keeps: an unsettled archive. The scandal stays allegations, and the mansion stays a source of Gothic and New Weird folklore, archival investigations, conspiracy claims and misleading clues - with no predetermined supernatural revelation.
dynasty.what_must_not_be_asserted: that the scandal is proven, or that the archive conceals any particular truth
evidence_classes: canon: the family and the firm existed

dynasty.role: the commercial facilitator of the 1964 transition
dynasty.what_the_scenario_keeps: a standing obligation with no owner. He facilitated a peaceful transition rather than bestowing it; the debt is inherited in both directions, and either side may call it in.
canon_invariants: British enterprises were negotiated into protection rather than expropriated
dynasty.what_must_not_be_asserted: that independence was granted by the Eldrich family, or that the CPU owes the firm anything not negotiated
evidence_classes: canon: the 1964 independence and its negotiated protections
interpretation: the moral weight of the bargain

dynasty.seat_note: Per the issue's MVP distinction he is initially an independent patron and major NPC, NOT automatically one of the libertarian party's four formal leaders. Placing him on a council would consume one of the four action slots under #323 and is the author's decision.
dynasty.what_the_scenario_keeps: an attention economy with a balance sheet: money, media, inventions, a space venture and a public party relationship that stays formally autonomous.
dynasty.what_must_not_be_asserted: that his Mars venture has already proven the ruins artificial, that stargates or anomalous transport exist, or that his patronage makes the libertarian party his instrument. In the present day his Mars project reads as publicity plus real engineering economics - launch cadence, insurance, freight, orbital logistics, contracts - and the scenario never has to tell the player whether he is right.
evidence_classes: canon: wealth, publicity, the party patronage, the Mars venture

leader_template.note: The concise shape every named leader record should satisfy. It matches the fields the twelve existing records in data/ukweli_local.json already use, plus one proposed addition that is NOT yet in the data.

proposed_addition.institutional_tie: which institution or network the seat is bound to, so a seat can be specified before a person is invented for it

not_in_this_template: any new statistic: the roster adds no score, rating or track
personality prose: bios are authored separately, and inventing individuals is forbidden here

portfolios.note: The four portfolios from #323, as already used by the existing leader records.
portfolios.rule: one persistent management portfolio per leader; a portfolio is passive and is never an extra active move

seats.note: The twelve existing leader seats, annotated with the institutional tie each needs. None carries a person: filling one is author work, not mine. Every entry points at an id that already exists in data/ukweli_local.json.

the port, industry and the state's resource base

uip.institutional_tie: the rural and communal representative bodies
land, agriculture and the coastal economy

ulp.institutional_tie: the party's parliamentary and populist opposition role
the enclave economy and offshore arrangements

independent_npcs.note: A handful of consequential independent NPCs are wanted by the issue, but no individual is invented here. The shape is specified and left empty, so a later pass can fill it without restructuring anything.
independent_npcs.already_covered_elsewhere: sir_mars_eldrich is an independent patron, and that record already exists as a canonical character card rather than being duplicated here

relationships.note: Tabular edges. Trust is a small signed value only where the existing data already carries one; no new quantity is invented.

edges.note: funds and publicly supports the party, which stays formally autonomous; derived from the landed character card, not restated from scratch
publicity is not endorsement, and reach is not votes
historical; the firm passes from the first generation to the second
the 1964 bargain is inherited in both directions; either side may call it in
patron of the opposition, and not sovereign over the port

event_hooks.note: The issue's candidate interactions, kept as invocable hooks rather than mechanics. Each names which historical generation it draws on, so a dead generation generates fiction without acting.

hooks.premise: leaked papers fuel competing discourses of liberation, pragmatism, colonial compromise and elite privilege.
hooks.strategic_shape: the interpretation of a past event is contested; the choices are about which reading the faction sponsors

hooks.premise: debate the legality of tax and offshore privileges, national jurisdiction and workers' protections.
hooks.strategic_shape: legitimacy, jobs, investment and party relations move together

hooks.premise: viral absurdity, a spectacular commercial promise or an intellectual-property scandal.
hooks.strategic_shape: publicity converts into media and political influence, with reputational risk

hooks.premise: a corporate space project competes with workers' demands or national infrastructure.
hooks.strategic_shape: a real, expensive, locally consequential commitment a government can tax, subsidise or nationalise the optics of

hooks.premise: ambiguous Victorian testimony and occult rumours create competing interpretations.
hooks.strategic_shape: no predetermined supernatural revelation; the archive may mislead

cautions: PROPOSAL ONLY. Nothing here is a locked rule, and no number above is approved.
Uranus and Mercury are historical and must stay invocable rather than agentic: they generate events, they do not compete for action slots.
Sir Mars Eldrich is already a landed canonical character card; this roster references it and does not restate or re-author it.

Allegations, satire, propaganda, established history and unresolved NHI/PSI mysteries must stay clearly distinguishable. The dynasty's evidence_classes fields exist so a claim cannot drift upward into canon by repetition.
No extra leader mission slots are introduced: the roster is four seats per faction, per #323.
The port is not sovereign territory: Eldrich's wealth affects but does not override gameplay.
